original_value: Although widely used in many applications, accurate and efficient human action recognition remains a challenging area of research in the field of computer vision. Most recent surveys have focused on narrow problems such as human action recognition methods using depth data, 3D-skeleton data, still image data, spatiotemporal interest point-based methods, and human walking motion recognition. However, there has been no systematic survey of human action recognition. To this end, we present a thorough review of human action recognition methods and provide a comprehensive overview of recent approaches in human action recognition research, including progress in hand-designed action features in RGB and depth data, current deep learning-based action feature representation methods, advances in human–object interaction recognition methods, and the current prominent research topic of action detection methods. Finally, we present several analysis recommendations for researchers. This survey paper provides an essential reference for those interested in further research on human action recognition.

result.paraphrase: Although human action recognition is widely applied, achieving accurate and efficient performance remains a difficult research problem in computer vision. Most recent surveys have concentrated on narrow topics, including methods based on depth data, 3D-skeleton data, still images, spatiotemporal interest points, and human walking motion recognition. Yet no systematic survey of human action recognition has been available. To address this gap, we offer a comprehensive review of human action recognition methods and an overview of recent research directions, covering progress in hand-crafted action features for RGB and depth data, current deep learning-based action feature representation methods, advances in human–object interaction recognition, and the increasingly important topic of action detection. We also provide several analytical recommendations for researchers. This survey paper serves as an important reference for anyone pursuing further study in human action recognition.
